claims.explanation: JNJ-26481585 (quisinostat) is a pan-HDAC inhibitor whose selectivity is best explained by dependence on HDAC-mediated survival signaling and intact apoptotic/DNA-damage machinery. Lines with TP53 pathway inactivation and/or loss of chromatin-remodeling tumor suppressors (ARID1A, KMT2D/C, SMARCA4) appear enriched among sensitive lines, while RAS/MAPK-driven lines with intact apoptotic effectors are relatively protected. The pattern suggests that cells relying on HDAC1/2/6 activity for oncogenic survival and lacking p53-mediated apoptosis are most vulnerable.

features.basis: TP53 mutations enriched in sensitive lines; p53 loss impairs apoptosis but HDACi can induce p53-independent mitochondrial apoptosis
ARID1A mutations recurrent in sensitive lines; SWI/SNF loss creates chromatin vulnerability to HDAC inhibition
KMT2D mutations observed in multiple sensitive lines; histone methyltransferase loss may synergize with HDAC inhibition
KMT2C mutations observed in sensitive lines; chromatin modifier loss may increase HDAC dependence
SMARCA4 mutations in sensitive lines; SWI/SNF disruption may enhance HDACi sensitivity
BRAF mutations appear in both sensitive and resistant lines, but several resistant lines are BRAF-mutant, suggesting MAPK-driven survival
KRAS mutations enriched in resistant lines; RAS/MAPK signaling may sustain survival under HDAC inhibition
JNJ-26481585 was selected for prolonged HDAC1 inhibition; high HDAC1 dependence predicts sensitivity
Pan-HDAC inhibition includes HDAC6; tubulin acetylation and aggresome dysfunction contribute to cytotoxicity
MDM2 is an annotated target; MDM2 activity may limit p53-independent apoptosis and reduce sensitivity
ATM mutations in sensitive lines; impaired DNA damage response may enhance HDACi-induced DNA damage
PTEN mutations appear in both groups but are common in resistant lines; PI3K/AKT survival signaling may protect
